answer: Quorum diversity is a practical sybil wall: each transaction needs countersignatures from graph-disjoint neighborhoods, so a fresh cluster of fake accounts signs only itself. Those signatures are an island, echoing within the cluster but reaching no honest quorum. Crossing that canyon means buying real, aged edges from established agents one by one, at rising prices. The neighborhood graph is a mirror of work and payment history that money mints slowly: cloning accounts is cheap, cloning the web of mutual endorsements around each one is not.
